transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Mitchell (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Lumina Head of Data), Ben Carter (CTO), Elena Ruiz (Security Lead), Samir Patel (ML Eng)
Shared: Redwood POC deck (link), Redwood security pack (placeholder link), Lumina data schema (requested)

Summary:
High-level POC scoping focusing on data handling requirements (PII, logging/redaction, retention, prompt storage) plus workload sizing for benchmarks and timeline to decision. Agreed next steps: share security artifacts, run benchmark, Lumina to provide sample prompts + PII tags, follow-up call to review results.

Topics:
- Success criteria for POC (latency, throughput, accuracy/regression bounds, cost)
- Workload sizing: QPS, token distribution, peak concurrency, typical session length
- Benchmarks: end-to-end with guarded sample data, redaction enabled, and with KV cache 
- Data handling: logging, prompt storage, PII redaction, retention policy, KMS/HSM encryption, audit logs, SSO/SAML
- Deployment preference: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intros, then we'll get into scope Diego and I from Redwood, and from Lumina I think Priya, Ben, Elena and Samir.
[00:18] Priya: Hi all, thanks. We're mainly focused on a short POC to validate that Redwood can meet our privacy and latency needs for patient-facing summarization flows.
[00:27] Ben: Quick background, we have a mix of internal microservices and an external web app. Peak concurrency around 120 concurrent users but bursts can go higher during morning syncs.
[00:40] Diego: Great, can you give rough QPS and token sizes? That'll help scope the bench.
[00:48] Samir: Typical request is 800-1,200 tokens in, and responses around 150-400 tokens. Avg QPS baseline is 6, peaks of 40 per second, but during batch jobs we might see sustained 100 QPS for short windows.
[01:05] Ava: Perfect, that's the kind of profile we need for sizing we'll propose a Dedicated pilot cluster vs hosted depending on results.
[01:14] Elena: On the security side, two non-negotiables: PII must not be stored in plaintext logs, and we need proof of encryption at rest with our KMS. Also audit logs for every request with user IDs masked.
[01:27] Diego: Understood. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for private deployments, and for hosted we provide AES-256 at rest with optional envelope encryption we also have a KMS integration guide.
[01:40] Priya: Is there an option to disable prompt storage entirely? We want to avoid retention of patient prompts beyond what's needed for debugging.
[01:49] Ava: Yes, we can configure retention. For POC we typically enable short-term retention for debugging (e.g., 7 days) and then use redaction hooks. We also offer a mode where prompts are not persisted effectively ephemeral requests but some features (like reranking or analytics) require retention.
[02:09] Ben: Can you walk through logging - what fields are logged and can we redact at ingest?
[02:17] Diego: Logs capture metadata (request id, model, latency), but content logging is opt-in. We have server-side redaction that can be configured to scrub patterns (SSNs, MRNs, PHI types). The redaction engine is rules + ML-assisted. Note: redaction isn't perfect so we recommend client-side pre-hash or tokenization for high-risk fields.
[02:41] Priya: Client-side hashing is doable for identifiers; we still need to test if that impacts model quality. We'll include de-hash mapping only in safe test environments.
[02:53] Ava: Good. For the POC success criteria let's capture it now: 1) average p95 latency under 400ms for short queries (<=256 tokens), 2) end-to-end throughput to support 100 sustained QPS with 95% availability during the run, 3) no PII persisted beyond configured retention and successful redaction on a 50-sample prompt set, 4) quality: Rouge-L/fidelity target comparable to current baseline within 5% (Lumina to provide eval set). Any additions?
[03:28] Ben: Add cost per 1M tokens estimate and an ops runbook for failover (fallback model) we need to know economics.
[03:37] Ava: We'll include cost projections and a fallback policy Redwood can route to a smaller model or a cached response on degradation.
[03:45] Samir: On prompt storage, curious about KV cache: does Redwood keep a per-session KV cache that might persist prompts? We need guarantees it won't leak across sessions.
[03:55] Diego: KV cache is ephemeral per session; it can be evicted immediately after session end. For Dedicated/Private we can control retention and caches at the infra level. Sometimes transcripts show up in support traces that's controllable by retention settings.
[04:13] Elena: We need audit logs for every admin action and key rotation events. Also SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[04:22] Ava: We support SAML SSO and SCIM. We'll share our SOC2 and ISO docs in the security pack.
[04:30] Priya: For the benchmark, we want two runs: (a) realistic traffic with redaction enabled, (b) identical traffic with redaction plus client-side hashing to measure model impact and latency delta.
[04:44] Diego: Makes sense. We'll provision a cluster for a 1-hour run with the exact token distribution you provided and collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, total throughput, and token/sec. We'll also capture cost estimates.
[04:58] Ben: How do you simulate our network constraints? We have clients in a VPC with egress limits.
[05:05] Diego: For Dedicated or Private, we can put the cluster in your VPC or set up a dedicated peering. For hosted tests we can run from a region that approximates your latency; results will differ slightly. We'll document network addendums in the test plan.
[05:22] Priya: On redaction, what's the false negative rate on your ML-assisted scrubber?
[05:28] Diego: We don't publish an absolute number because it depends on training data; we do provide a QA report per run. For regulated data we recommend client-side redaction combined with our server-side policies.
[05:38] Elena: Can you confirm that for hosted we can enable customer-managed keys (CMK)?
[05:43] Ava: Hosted offers envelope encryption with customer-provided CMKs for an enterprise plan. Private/Dedicated naturally integrates with your KMS. We'll include exact steps in the security pack.
[05:56] Samir: Timeline how soon can we run the benchmark? We're aiming to make a decision in 3 weeks.
[06:02] Ava: If you share the sample prompts and PII tags by 2025-09-19, we can provision a cluster and run the benchmark the week of 2025-09-22 and have results ready within 3 business days after the run.
[06:14] Ben: Sounds good. Any limits on the eval samples we can send? We want to include edge cases and red-team style examples.
[06:22] Diego: No strict limits, but for the controlled run keep it to ~500 unique prompts to make the run manageable. Include the high-risk edge cases flagged by your security team.
[06:34] Priya: About storing prompts for debugging can we hash the full prompt and store only the hash + small debug snippet?
[06:41] Diego: Yes, that's a common pattern store hash + redacted snippet. We can also provide a debug key to reconstitute only in the private test environment.
[06:52] Elena: Auditability we need to demonstrate for auditors that data retention rules were enforced. Do you provide retention logs?
[06:59] Ava: Yes, we emit retention lifecycle events to audit logs. We'll include sample retention logs in the security pack.
[07:08] Ben: For the success criteria around quality, we'll provide a baseline eval run and the metrics we care about.
[07:14] Priya: Also can you show us worst-case tail latency numbers? We care about p99 and p999 for SLA planning.
[07:21] Diego: We'll capture p50/p95/p99/p999. For p999 you may need a larger run; we'll discuss sampling strategies in the test plan.
[07:33] Ava: Recap of next steps: Redwood share security pack + KMS guide; Lumina share prompt-set & PII tags; Redwood schedule benchmark and test plan; follow-up meet after results.
[07:44] Ben: I'll loop in procurement we might need an NDA amendment for the sample data.
[07:50] Elena: I'll send our compliance questionnaire; expecting answers in the security pack.
[07:56] Priya: One more thing can you demonstrate redaction on a few live examples in the POC?
[08:01] Diego: Yes, we can run a small live demo during the benchmark or as a separate session.
[08:08] Ava: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send the artifacts and proposed schedule by end of day Friday.
